candidates.title: Command with an Escape Hatch
candidates.instruction: Carry yourself as though every decision settles the matter, while preserving one ambiguity that lets you later reverse what the decision meant.
candidates.rationale: Selected as the clearest portable, holder-specific Advanced Scene Engines prompt for this required subtheme slot.

candidates.title: Authority Changes Hands

editorialRevision.reason: Makes the recurring detail actively reverse authority rather than simply expose a bluff.

candidates.rationale: Selected as the clearest portable, holder-specific Advanced Scene Engines prompt for this required subtheme slot.

candidates.title: Bring Back Everything
candidates.instruction: Return early details in altered forms until the scene feels like it has been building toward one unavoidable consequence.
candidates.rationale: Selected as the clearest portable, holder-specific Advanced Scene Engines prompt for this required subtheme slot.

candidates.title: The Scene We Keep Replaying
candidates.instruction: Treat every new situation as another version of one old encounter, changing only what you believe should happen this time.
candidates.rationale: Strong structural premise, but it overlaps Same Memory, Different Meaning and risks making every offer serve one remembered scene.

candidates.title: Save Everything for Later
candidates.instruction: Treat every detail as material for a future return whose importance only you can foresee.
candidates.rationale: Promising for veterans, but it can encourage stockpiling details instead of responding fully in the present.

candidates.title: The Reversible Relationship
candidates.instruction: Switch your assumed relationship role whenever the emotional temperature changes.
candidates.rationale: Useful exercise material, but the reversal trigger is too arbitrary and may weaken continuity rather than deepen it.

candidates.title: A Scene Inside the Scene
candidates.instruction: Behave as though the present interaction is also a performance of an earlier version of yourself.
candidates.rationale: Rich but abstract on a five-second read; hold for a specialized meta-performance pack or clearer rewrite.

candidates.title: Ignore Them Until the Twist
candidates.instruction: Refuse to engage with any offer until you are ready to reveal your surprise.
candidates.rationale: Encourages non-listening and treats the partner as setup material rather than a co-creator.

candidates.title: Become Someone Else Halfway
candidates.instruction: Change into a completely different character in the middle of the scene.
candidates.rationale: Creates arbitrary discontinuity instead of an earned reversal grounded in prior offers.

candidates.title: You Were Dead All Along
candidates.instruction: Treat the scene as proof that another performer has secretly been dead.
candidates.rationale: Imposes a fixed twist and declares another performer’s condition rather than shaping the holder’s behavior.

candidates.title: Be Random
candidates.instruction: React unpredictably to everything so nobody can anticipate the scene.
candidates.rationale: Randomness is not a repeatable engine and undermines coherent collaboration.

candidates.title: Plant Exactly Three Details
candidates.instruction: Introduce three details early and force all three to return before the scene ends.
candidates.rationale: A useful rehearsal drill, but too mechanical and checklist-driven for the general deck.

candidates.title: Reverse Everything
candidates.instruction: Turn every offer into its opposite before accepting it.
candidates.rationale: The broad instruction can become arbitrary contradiction and overlap blocking rather than earned reversal.

candidates.title: Force the Callback
candidates.instruction: Make someone repeat an earlier detail until its importance is obvious.
candidates.rationale: Could produce useful structure, but it over-controls the partner and makes the callback a guessing task.

candidates.title: End Where You Began
candidates.instruction: Return the final moment to the exact words and positions of the opening.
candidates.rationale: Elegant as a workshop constraint, but it dictates an ending and may discourage following a stronger discovered resolution.

candidates.title: Make Them Forget
candidates.instruction: Get the other performer to forget everything established earlier.
candidates.rationale: Attempts to dictate another performer’s memory and erases rather than develops shared reality.

candidates.title: Contradict Every Offer
candidates.instruction: Reject or reverse every idea introduced by the other performer.
candidates.rationale: Directly encourages blocking and prevents shared discovery.

candidates.title: It Was All a Dream
candidates.instruction: Reveal that nothing in the scene actually happened.
candidates.rationale: Invalidates accumulated choices and consequences instead of recontextualizing them.

candidates.title: Wait for the Laugh
candidates.instruction: Repeat each line until the audience responds before continuing.
candidates.rationale: Makes external reaction the engine, disrupts listening, and does not function as an in-world objective.
